headline: Solid timing — your lower body is where the story is.

sections.title: What lined up well
sections.body: Your tempo (3.35 : 1) sits right in the tour range, and the pieces of your upper-body coil match too: shoulder turn at the top (40.4°), X-factor (22.3°) and spine tilt at address (32.6°) are all inside the typical tour band. That's a repeatable foundation.

sections.title: The main thing that stood out
sections.body: Your hips were much more open at impact (46.7°) than the tour range (10–24°), while your lateral weight shift (0.16%) measured well below the tour band (0.5–1.6%). Together that reads as rotation without much lateral drive — the hips spin open but don't move toward the target first.

sections.title: Also worth a look
sections.body: Your head moved sideways more than most tour swings — 57.6% of body scale against a typical 20–40% band.

sections.title: One we left out
sections.body: Lead-arm extension measured 121.3°, but wrist depth is hard to see from this camera angle, so we treat that number as low-confidence and didn't factor it into the read.
